text:
zoe: quick sync on fallback billing + rate safety. we need a compact, defensible behavior for requests that pin a premium model but get routed to a cheaper compatible model. thoughts?
dmitri: enumerate options quickly? i'm juggling oncall.
zoe: short list: 1) always bill requested model (we eat cost), 2) bill effective model (tenant pays less), 3) bill requested but track fallbacks and apply credits later.
harper: variant idea: bill requested but maintain a tenant-level "fallback allowance" (burst budget) that pays for N tokens of fallback per minute. beyond that -> degraded path enforcement. keeps predictability but limits abuse.
kai: that allowance idea seems promising. what's the budget shape? fixed tokens? leaky-bucket?
harper: recommend leaky-bucket: refill R tokens/sec, capacity B. fallback consumes token proportional to tokens_generated_by_effective_model. if bucket empty -> we either queue, probabilistic reject, or require explicit downgrade.
dmitri: leaky-bucket is standard. two questions: (a) how to pick R and B per tenant (uniform vs percent-of-quota) and (b) how quickly do we surface to customers?
zoe: propose defaults: R = min( max(1 request/sec, quota_tokens_per_minute * 0.02), 5000 tokens/sec) and B = R * 60 (one minute burst). for heavy enterprise tenants allow overrides via support.
kai: fuzzy: use percent-of-active-commit so that big commit customers get proportional allowance. small free-tier gets tiny R which prevents gaming.
harper: enforcement modes: "soft" = tag response + emit metric, "hard" = start probabilistic rejects with p increasing to 1 as bucket deficit grows, "visible downgrade" = flip tenant into explicit fallback mode and show console banner.
infra-bot: metric: fallback_tokens_consumed=17890 tenant=widgetco window=60s bucket_level=-320 alert=warn
dmitri: we should avoid surprise billing or silent quality regressions. recommended rollout: start with soft tagging + tenant dashboard, then opt-in hard enforcement for 2 weeks, then enable automatic visible downgrade at threshold.
zoe: agree. billing policy: no automatic refunds. Instead, sustained fallback above threshold (e.g., average bucket deficit > 30% for 3h) triggers manual review and potential credit. automating refunds invites gaming.
kai: telemetry detail: require ingress to emit fields: requested_model, effective_model, fallback_reason, token_count. store both model ids in event stream. add a small per-tenant time-series for bucket_level.
harper: anti-gaming probes: detect pattern of start/stop bursts that align with window boundaries, correlate IP/caller-id, and compute per-caller fallback ratio. if a single API key drives >75% of fallbacks mark for review.
dmitri: also rate-limit fallback credit consumption at the admission layer so that other tenants' SLOs are preserved. if host-level load high -> deny fallback requests earlier.
zoe: ops checklist for rollout: [x] ingress headers/events (requested_model,effective_model,reason,tokens) [ ] metrics pipeline: ingest bucket_level timeseries [ ] dashboard widget: tenant fallback chart [ ] console banner plumbing [ ] admission-layer fallback gating hook
infra-bot: task created: #infra-1234 create bucket metric with 1s resolution, 48h retention
harper: follow-ups: i'll draft a short RFC describing bucket math, default R/B, deficit -> probability curve for rejects, and the escalation playbook. include sample telemetry queries and alert thresholds.
kai: i'll prototype admission hook for probabilistic reject: p = clamp( (deficit / B), 0, 1 ). open PR after RFC.
dmitri: we should document customer-facing wording: "Fallback allowance" and "Visible fallback mode". tone: transparent, explain quality implications.
zoe: decision summary: implement leaky-bucket fallback allowance per-tenant, start with soft tagging + dashboards, no automated refunds, manual credit path for sustained deficits, and an admission-layer gate for host protection. RFC + PRs targeted this week.
harper: will ping when RFC draft is up.
zoe: thanks all. ping if you see weird spikes during the test rollout tonight. :rocket:
